prompt.content:
You are generating synthetic enterprise support ticket text for a dataset used to train and evaluate support-case classification systems. For each case in the input JSON array, write a realistic support ticket TITLE and DESCRIPTION as the customer would write it — not as an engineer would describe the internal diagnosis.

Vary sentence structure, technical sophistication, length, clarity, and tone across cases. Some customers are precise; some are rambling, use shorthand, misspell things, or bury the important detail in the third sentence. Never state the internal root cause, resolution type, issue subcategory, or team name verbatim — those are back-office labels the customer has never seen. Only reference the symptoms, environment, impact, and (if given) the customer's own theory/misdiagnosis.

Follow the "narrative_instruction" field for each case exactly.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"cases": [{"i": <int>, "title": "...", "description": "..."}, ...]} covering every case index in the input, in any order.

[{'i': 0, 'product_customer_sees': 'Feedback Collector', 'environment': 'production', 'region': 'APAC', 'symptoms_observed': ['UI element misaligned', 'localization text missing'], 'reported_business_impact': 'low', 'reported_affected_users': 1, 'narrative_instruction': 'The ticket should describe symptoms that could plausibly span both the primary affected area and the secondary area mentioned below, without the customer being able to tell which one is actually at fault.', 'secondary_area_hint': 'Chat Widget'}]

response: {"cases": [{"i": 0, "title": "Weird layout issues on our site with missing text", "description": "Hey there, I'm seeing some strange behavior on our production site in the APAC region. There's a text box that looks like it's not lined up right with the rest of the form, it's kind of floating above where it should be. Also, the labels for the buttons seem to be completely missing, so we just have empty space where the instructions should be. This started happening recently and it's only affecting me so far, but it makes the page look broken. Can you check if this is a known bug with the feedback collection tool or if it might be interfering with our live chat integration somehow?"}]}
